_comment: Enumerated request-shape typing debt, checked by `pnpm check:request-shapes`.
Every entry is a field the guard WOULD flag, kept with a reason rather than typed today.
An entry that matches nothing FAILS the check — pay the debt, delete the line.
Adding an entry is a deliberate act: prefer typing the field.

`methodParams` enumerates the engine-method parameter keys (`method.key`) still typed bare any, each with a code from `methodParamReasons`. It may only shrink: a typed key that regresses is not on it and fails.

allow.TransitionRecordStatusArgs.record: Deliberately generic — the function transitions a status on ANY record in ANY collection, keyed by collectionKey/idKey. A narrower type would defeat its purpose.
allow.CallListenerArgs.payloads: Subscription payloads are topic-shaped and provider-defined; the factory does not constrain what a subscriber receives.
allow.CallListenerArgs.notices: Deprecated back-compat alias for payloads, slated for removal in a future major. Typing a field on its way out is wasted motion.
allow.HandleCaughtErrorArgs.params: The arbitrary argument object of whichever engine method threw.
allow.HandleCaughtErrorArgs.err: A caught value. TypeScript types `catch` bindings as `unknown` or `any` by design and this is that value.
allow.AddCourtsArgs.courtTimings: Per-court timing overrides, indexed by court ordinal (addCourt.ts:166) and spread into a per-date availability object, so the shape is whatever the caller supplies. `addCourts` is a PUBLIC engine method (factoryEngineMethods.ts, venueGovernor/mutate.ts), so typing it would both invent a contract that was never authored and be a consumer-build break. An earlier reason here claimed the mocks surface was the only producer — that was wrong, and being public is the stronger argument for authoring the shape deliberately rather than inferring it.
allow.BuildTournamentRecordArgs.eventDataDocs: Raw provider documents from an external source system. The builder's contract is that it accepts whatever the source emits.

methodParamReasons.guardTest: The method's own tests pass deliberately invalid or partial values for this key to exercise its validation; a typed key would need those tests to cast.
methodParamReasons.validator: A validator's input is by contract potentially invalid: the honest type is unknown, and the body reads it as a record without narrowing, so typing it means rewriting the body around runtime checks.
methodParamReasons.catalogue: Callers pass the catalogue's tie formats, which are untyped JSON; typing the key waits on the catalogue exporting typed tie formats.
methodParamReasons.model: The model type this key would take is narrower than the values the body reads (or the body reads a union without narrowing), so typing it means changing the model type or the body, not the parameter.
methodParamReasons.callerShape: Two internal callers assemble this argument with different shapes and no declared type; typing it means declaring that row shape first.
methodParamReasons.openShape: Caller-defined per-court overrides spread into the court availability; the same open shape as AddCourtsArgs.courtTimings.
methodParamReasons.dynamicRead: The body copies the value attribute by attribute under names it reads at runtime; typed as a Partial of the record, each of those reads is an implicit any, so typing it means typing that attribute walk.
methodParamReasons.unguarded: Typed, the body would need a non-null assertion that no guard in the function supports: it reads an optional field of the record (or of a found element) as present on a path where nothing rules out its absence. Typing it honestly needs a runtime guard, which this types-only pass does not add.
